text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Egyptian President Mubarak calls for shared prosperity at Cairo conference.
- U.S. Ambassador Indyk hosts top-level bid for Hebron deal.
- Foreign Minister Levy demands Azam Azam's release.
- United States: Gaza industrial park to operate in two months.
- Three Israel firms among European Easdaq market founders.
- Elbit's net income climbs 7.8 percent.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Hebron Agreement expected today. Israeli army work plan: Hebron pullback this coming weekend.
- "Spy in Cairo" story: Netanyahu passed a biting message to Egyptian President Mubarak.
- Son of Hebron killer Baruch Goldstein blessed on his Bar Mitzvah: "Follow the path of your father the hero."
- Settlers request meeting with Palestinians in Hebron.
HAARETZ
- Christopher pressures Israel and Palestinian Authority to finish Hebron agreement today.
- Political sources: 'Azam is not a spy. Egypt is trying to halt business with Israel.'
- Israel Army considers turning Hebron over on sabbath.
- Estimates: Scitex will post an $80 million loss in Q3.
- Tnuva in contacts to purchase information and cooperate with food giant Kraft.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu works to enlist support of chief rabbis on Hebron redeployment.
- Israel to United States: help free spy suspect from Egypt.
- Poll: 60 percent of Israelis suspect outbreak of war.
GLOBES
- Israeli businessmen report: dejected atmosphere at Cairo conference.
- Income tax authorities recommend first charges in News Datacom against Leo Krieger.
- Osem-Tivol group in contacts to buy Hod-Lavan.
